entities.name: Petronius Annianus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Petronius Annianus was a Roman aristocrat of the Constantinian age who reached the ordinary consulship in 314 CE alongside Imp. Caesar Flavius Constantinus Augustus, signalling the reassembly of senatorial prestige after the Tetrarchic civil wars.

As a member of the Petronii, he occupied high civilian office alongside other prominent families, including the Anii and the Caesonii, as Constantine fused imperial monarchy with traditional honorific cursus.

His consulship belongs to the years when Constantine, newly dominant in the West after the Milvian Bridge, used consular appointments to reinforce his authority and establish a new imperial system.

Petronius Annianus's legacy extends to the later Roman Empire, where he is remembered as a key figure in the reassembly of senatorial prestige.

The Petronii's influence can be seen in the Roman aristocracy's continued struggles for power and influence, even as the empire began to fracture and collapse.

In the 5th century CE, the Petronii would continue to play a significant role in the politics of the Western Roman Empire, as the family's fortunes waxed and waned in the face of shifting power dynamics.

In the end, Petronius Annianus's consulship represents a fleeting moment of senatorial prestige, a brief respite from the Tetrarchic civil wars that would eventually shatter the Roman Empire's social and political fabric.
